Register models from a CSV file

Source: R/core-transport-models-file.R
hr_load_models.Rd

Reads a file of models and registers each row as hr_register_model() would. Use it to set the prices of many models at once: harnessr ships each built-in model's limits but no prices, because providers change prices more often than the package is released.

Usage

hr_load_models(file)

Arguments

file

Path to the CSV file.

Value

Invisibly, the ids registered, in file order.

File format

A CSV file with a header row and one row per model. Only id is required; a blank cell, or NA, means the value is not given.

id

The model id, exactly as the API expects it. Each id may appear once.

input_usd, output_usd

Price per 1M tokens, in USD. Give both for a chat model, or neither. An embedding model needs only input_usd.

cached_input_usd

Price per 1M input tokens served from the provider's prompt cache. Blank prices them as other input tokens.

as_of

The month the prices were checked, as YYYY-MM. Blank stamps the current month, and a month after the current one is an error. A row that gives only some of a priced model's prices keeps the older month, since the prices it leaves out are as old as before. A cost computed from prices older than hr_options("price_max_age_days") warns with class hr_stale_price, once per model per session.

context_window, max_output

Limits in tokens.

reasoning, supports_temperature

TRUE or FALSE.

kind

chat or embedding.

dimensions

Embedding dimensions, for an embedding model.

A row that gives both context_window and max_output registers the model in full, and a blank column takes hr_register_model()'s default. A row that leaves either limit blank changes the model's current entry, built in or registered, and keeps every value the row leaves blank. So a row with only id, input_usd and output_usd prices a built-in model and keeps its limits:


id,input_usd,output_usd,as_of
gpt-4o,2.50,10.00,2026-11
my-local-llama,0,0,2026-11

The second row works only if my-local-llama is already registered.

harnessr checks the whole file before it registers anything. A file it cannot use stops with an error of class hr_bad_models_file that names the row and column at fault (row 1 is the first row after the header) and carries them as the condition's row and column fields; the registry is then left as it was.

See also

hr_register_model() for one model, hr_models() to check the result, hr_estimate_cost()

Other cost and token functions: hr_budget(), hr_context_fit(), hr_context_policy(), hr_count_tokens(), hr_estimate_cost(), hr_model_info(), hr_model_limits(), hr_models(), hr_register_model(), hr_set_tokenizer(), hr_tokenizer(), hr_truncate(), hr_truncate_tokens()

Examples

# The prices here are illustrative: use your provider's current prices.
# With no as_of column, the prices are stamped with the current month.
prices <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c("id,input_usd,output_usd",
             "gpt-4o,2.50,10.00",
             "gpt-4o-mini,0.15,0.60"), prices)
hr_load_models(prices)
m <- hr_models()
m[m$id %in% c("gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini"),
  c("id", "context_window", "input_usd_per_1m", "output_usd_per_1m", "as_of")]
#>            id context_window input_usd_per_1m output_usd_per_1m   as_of
#> 7      gpt-4o         128000             2.50              10.0 2026-11
#> 8 gpt-4o-mini         128000             0.15               0.6 2026-11

# A malformed file names the row and column, and registers nothing.
writeLines(c("id,input_usd,output_usd", "gpt-4o,two,10"), prices)
tryCatch(hr_load_models(prices), hr_bad_models_file = conditionMessage)
#> [1] "Models file '/tmp/RtmpVwNvOF/file1bfe4b01cb1b.csv', row 1, column 'input_usd': 'two' is not a price; give USD per 1M tokens as a number of 0 or more, such as 2.5."
unlink(prices)
